subsystems.name: Source
subsystems.role: injects carriers into the channel by quantum tunnelling rather than by thermal emission.

subsystems.name: Channel
subsystems.role: the region between source and drain whose energy barrier is controlled by the gate.

subsystems.name: Drain
subsystems.role: collects the tunnelled carriers and passes them to the interconnect.

subsystems.name: Gate stack
subsystems.role: applies an electric field that aligns the energy bands so tunnelling can occur at low voltage.

subsystems.name: Tunnel barrier
subsystems.role: the engineered interface where band-to-band tunnelling takes place.

buildSteps.title: Choose the material system
buildSteps.detail: Select semiconductors with suitable band alignment — for example a broken-gap pair such as InAs and GaSb, or a staggered-gap pair such as germanium on silicon — so that the valence and conduction bands overlap when biased.

buildSteps.title: Grow the layers
buildSteps.detail: Use molecular beam epitaxy or chemical vapour deposition to deposit ultra-thin layers with atomic precision on a silicon or III-V substrate.

buildSteps.title: Dope the source
buildSteps.detail: Introduce very high concentrations of dopants, by ion implantation or in-situ during growth, to create a degenerate source region.

buildSteps.title: Pattern the device
buildSteps.detail: Use electron-beam or extreme-ultraviolet lithography to define the source, channel and gate areas.

buildSteps.title: Deposit the gate stack
buildSteps.detail: Grow a high-k dielectric by atomic layer deposition, then deposit a metal gate on top.

buildSteps.title: Form contacts
buildSteps.detail: Deposit metals such as nickel or titanium and anneal to make low-resistance contacts to the source and drain.

buildSteps.title: Isolate and interconnect
buildSteps.detail: Etch isolation trenches, fill them with oxide, and build multi-level metal wiring to connect the transistors.

buildSteps.title: Characterise
buildSteps.detail: Measure current–voltage curves, subthreshold swing and on/off ratio to verify that tunnelling switches the device below the thermal limit.

prerequisites.why: growing defect-free III-V or germanium layers directly on silicon is difficult and defect states degrade tunnelling.

prerequisites.tech: Atomic layer deposition of high-k dielectrics
prerequisites.why: the gate stack must be thin, uniform and free of traps to control the tunnel barrier precisely.
abrupt, highly doped junctions are needed for efficient band-to-band tunnelling.
materials such as molybdenum disulfide or black phosphorus can form atomically sharp junctions with no dangling bonds.
contact resistance often dominates the total resistance and masks the low-voltage switching benefit.

pathway.milestone: silicon-based tunnelling transistors show sub-60 mV/decade switching in laboratories, but only at very low currents
pathway.unlocks: proof that the thermal limit of conventional transistors can be beaten.

pathway.milestone: III-V heterojunction devices reach higher on-currents while keeping steep switching
pathway.unlocks: performance close to that needed for logic circuits.

pathway.milestone: two-dimensional material tunnelling transistors with abrupt, defect-free junctions
pathway.unlocks: scalable devices that can be stacked in three dimensions.
battery-limited and energy-harvesting electronics that run for years without replacement.
